#### 1. semantic dementia  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.732)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-264870, Reactome:R-HSA-9619483, Reactome:R-HSA-9833482)

**Proposed mechanism:** MAPT variant (rsXXXXXX) —DISRUPTS→ MAPT (HGNC:6893); MAPT (HGNC:6893) —INCREASES→ Tau hyperphosphorylation and aggregation (GO:0008210); Tau hyperphosphorylation and aggregation (GO:0008210) —LEADS_TO→ Neurodegeneration (HP:0002093); Tau hyperphosphorylation and aggregation (GO:0008210) —LEADS_TO→ Progressive supranuclear palsy-parkinsonism syndrome (MONDO:0009839); PSEN1 variant (rsYYYYYY) —DISRUPTS→ PSEN1 (HGNC:9190); PSEN1 (HGNC:9190) —DISRUPTS→ Amyloid precursor protein processing (REACT:R-HSA-1938635); Amyloid precursor protein processing (REACT:R-HSA-1938635) —LEADS_TO→ Neurodegeneration (HP:0002093); Amyloid precursor protein processing (REACT:R-HSA-1938635) —LEADS_TO→ Semantic dementia (MONDO:0010857). Mutations in MAPT lead to aberrant tau processing and aggregation, causing neurodegeneration and PSP-parkinsonism. Similarly, mutations in PSEN1 disrupt APP processing, leading to toxic amyloid species, neurodegeneration, and semantic dementia. Both pathways converge on the common downstream phenotype of neurodegeneration.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of pathogenic variants in MAPT in individuals with PSP-parkinsonism syndrome, or absence of pathogenic variants in PSEN1 in individuals with semantic dementia, would weaken this hypothesis. Furthermore, if studies demonstrate that the tauopathy and amyloidogenic pathways are completely independent and do not interact at any level leading to shared downstream effects, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: High frequency (>1%) of known pathogenic variants for either MAPT or PSEN1 in the general population (gnomAD).)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared downstream impact of distinct upstream genetic defects (tauopathy vs. amyloidogenesis) on neurodegeneration could reveal common therapeutic targets for these and other related neurodegenerative disorders, potentially impacting treatments for both Alzheimer's disease spectrum disorders and tauopathies.
